escena: SCENE (cinematic still, Hollywood drama, a vast dark contemporary archive room at night, a faint trace of haze only on the right of the frame, a cool frame, no people anywhere): a low shot across a long matte black reading table. ONE long index-card drawer has been pulled fully out of a tall card-catalog cabinet and rests open on the far end of the table, seen almost END-ON: its near end faces the camera squarely and its length runs straight away from the lens, so the whole drawer is a narrow shape between 64 % and 82 % of the frame width and NOTHING of it extends to the left of 64 % of the frame width. Drawer and cabinets are contemporary: matte black-stained ash with a fine, even grain, no varnish shine, flush recessed finger pulls, no brass, no label holders. Behind the drawer, on the right, a wall of identical cabinets several metres long recedes into the darkness of the archive. Inside the drawer stand HUNDREDS of identical thick, bright cool-white index cards packed upright, tightly, edge to edge, their top edges forming one long even ridge. The camera stands about two and a half metres from the drawer, low, its lens only a few centimetres behind the near edge of the table and at the height of the card tops, tilted very slightly down, 85mm f/2.8. The bare matte black tabletop fills the whole lower half of the frame as one calm, even, dark surface receding toward the drawer. Near the middle of the drawer, at about 74 % of the frame width, exactly ONE card stands raised halfway out of the pack, pulled up and left standing, clearly above all the others, its lower half still held between its neighbours. It is small in the frame, about one tenth of the frame width. Its top edge sits about one fifth of the way down from the top of the frame, and the long even line of card tops sits just below it, at about one quarter of the frame height. Between the left edge of the frame and the drawer there is a wide band of empty darkness about two thirds of the frame wide; the drawer, the raised card and every lit thing stay to the right of 64 % of the frame width and below the top fifth of the frame. That raised card is the brightest thing in the frame: the narrow spotlight from above falls only on it, so its upper half glows clean cold white with a soft falloff, and a thin rim of light catches its top edge. The cards right next to it catch only a faint grey glint on their top edges; every other card falls off into deep shadow along the drawer. The light carries the colour of the line: the centre of the pool is cold white, and its soft edge, where it falls off across the raised card and onto the top edges of its neighbours, turns saturated azure-blue (#0375DB): the only colour in the frame, a thin fringe, never a glow that floods the scene. All the cards are PLAIN and BLANK: NO handwriting, NO typed text, NO lines, NO ruled lines, NO numbers, NO tabs with letters, NO guide cards, NO divider tabs, NO labels, NO stamps, NO symbols and NO marks; the drawer front has NO label card and NO letter. There is no hand, no person, no device, no screen. There is no face anywhere in this frame: wherever the lighting notes speak of a face, they mean the raised card, its lit upper half against the deep shadow of its neighbours. The materials are contemporary and well kept: crisp clean card stock with sharp corners, matte black-stained ash with a fine even grain, no dust, no yellowing, no wear, nothing vintage, nothing sepia, nothing warm, amber or golden, no tungsten glow. The whole frame is cool and contemporary. In that haze, the spotlight draws one thin vertical shaft of azure-white light straight down onto the raised card, entirely between 70 % and 78 % of the frame width; nothing of it leans toward the left of the frame. Above the table and the drawer, the LEFT 64 % of the frame is calm, deep dark space: no light and no objects, no bokeh, no beams. No books, no lamps, no plants, no papers on top, no monitors. Enormous contrast, no readable text anywhere, no logos of any brand.
